Data:Painting.sky.json.Label: 'Self-Born'
Data:Painting.sky.json.Desc: A furry, cloven-looking foot reaches towards a mirror: its reflection is a bird's claw.

Data:Painting.teeny2.json.Label: 'Crowcross Sands at High Tide'
Data:Painting.teeny2.json.Desc: A gloomy study of the sea in gloomy weather.

xexts.scrutiny: Barely visible at the painting's edge, there are floating timbers that suggest a wrecked fishing boat…

Data:Painting.teeny3.json.Label: 'The Boy Prays'
Data:Painting.teeny3.json.Desc: There's no sign of a boy in this distorted, menacing image, and no-one seems to be praying.

xexts.scrutiny: In the darkness gathering at the back, a crowd of eyes might suggest a pack of hounds…

Data:Painting.thecalm.json.Label: 'Sedona, Not Yet'
Data:Painting.thecalm.json.Desc: One of Dr Levinsen's 'prefigures', an impossible copy of a painting that the real artist hadn't yet executed. He's signed it with the Illumination mark, and dated it '1958'.

xexts.scrutiny: At this very moment, perhaps, Max Ernst is dreaming of Arizona. But he hasn't painted this yet.

Data:Painting.thekiss.json.Label: 'Again, at Night'
Data:Painting.thekiss.json.Desc: One of Dr Levinsen's 'prefigures', a close (and impossible) copy of a painting made twenty years later by Kirchner, whose work Levinsen often anticipated in his mirror-dreams.

Data:Painting.tree.teeny.json.Label: 'Leaves in the Wind'
Data:Painting.tree.teeny.json.Desc: A soothing but undistinguished work in oils. Someone evidently was good at trees, and wanted you to know it.

xexts.scrutiny: In the foreground, an odd curl of shadow might just be a hand reaching from a crevice in a yew-tree trunk.

Data:Painting.tryphon.json.Label: 'Lady Tryphon'
Data:Painting.tryphon.json.Desc: A very old portrait in the Byzantine style.

xexts.scrutiny: A handwritten card tucked into the frame reads 'Sequester on sight. - G.C'

Data:Painting.winter.json.Label: 'Supplication'
Data:Painting.winter.json.Desc: The Sun-in Rags, but reversed, that is, blood is dripping down into the sun and being absorbed.

Data:Pale.mommet.json.Label: Pale Mommet
Data:Pale.mommet.json.Desc: A gently twitching little cloth doll with melancholy button eyes and a frill of coloured ribbons.

xexts.scrutiny: It's cold. It's always cold. It's grateful for my warmth… [There are Scholar-level Grail recipes which can craft one of these from fabric.]

Data:Parchment.anthropoderm.json.Label: Hallowed Anthropoderm
Data:Parchment.anthropoderm.json.Desc: Yes, it's human skin, but it's not just human skin.

xexts.scrutiny: Blessed by the priests of the Thunderskin, in those hollows of time where the Thunderskin is honoured for his work of preservation…

Data:Parchment.nivine.json.Label: Nivine Parchment
Data:Parchment.nivine.json.Desc: Pale as the first wisp of mountain-cloud.

xexts.scrutiny: What animal gave its skin to make this parchment? Something colourless as glass and snow; something bleached and wrung and purer than silence.

Data:Payment.json.label: Payment
Data:Payment.json.desc: Currently, this just removes the entire coin. With some extra behaviour, it should give change.

Data:Pear.belle.helene.json.Label: Poire Belle Hélène
Data:Pear.belle.helene.json.Desc: A sweet dish named (of course) to celebrate Offenbach's 1865 operetta La belle Hélène. Apparently a New York production made an impression on Thirza Blake in her youth…

xexts.scrutiny: In one folktale, the Witch prophesied to the Sister that the sea would drink her blood; the Sister prophesied to the Witch that the sea would never harm her. When they came ashore by Brancrug, she gave her a shell to catch rainwater in, and the sharp edge shed her blood on the white sand. That blood we know as rose-pearls.

Data:Pears.ys.json.Label: Poires Ys
Data:Pears.ys.json.Desc: Like Poire Belle Hélène, except it makes you dream of drowned sunsets.

Data:Pence.json.label: Pence
Data:Pence.json.desc: The eccentric currency of a fallen empire. One penny is four farthings, twelve pence are one shilling, and so on.

Data:Penny.json.label: Penny
Data:Penny.json.desc: The smallest denomination coin, except for the smaller ones.

Data:Perhibiate.json.Label: Perhibiate
Data:Perhibiate.json.Desc: Which binds to the one whose name is there written. A minor Ink of Power.

xexts.scrutiny: And so my name be not forgotten… [Perhibiate can be crafted with certain Prentice-leve Heart recipes.]

Data:Perinculate.json.Label: Perinculate
Data:Perinculate.json.Desc: Deadly. Use gloves to read texts produced with this pigment. An Ink of Power (sometimes considered an Unsanctioned Ink).

xexts.scrutiny: Perilous indeed. [There are Scholar-level Edge recipes that can craft this from leaves.]

Data:Period.baronial.json.label: Baronial Period
Data:Period.baronial.json.desc: In the 16th Century, the Dewulf family became the Barons Brancrug, governing the Isle as their personal estate - until 1759, when their line ended in madness and death.

Data:Period.curia.json.label: Curia Period
Data:Period.curia.json.desc: In the 18th century, a secretive cabal of scholars established the 'Curia of the Isle' to manage Hush House, making it a haven of knowledge until 1896 when a disgraced Librarian brought the House to penury.

Data:Period.dawn.json.label: Dawn Period
Data:Period.dawn.json.desc: 599 AD is the traditional date of the first foundation here, sometimes called the Abbey of the Black Dove, sometimes the Abbey of the White Crow... but the Sisterhood of the Triple Knot first built their temples here much earlier than that.

Data:Period.nocturnal.json.label: Nocturnal Period
Data:Period.nocturnal.json.desc: By the beginning of the 20th century, an unwise Librarian's enthusiasms had brought Hush House to penury. Nocturnal Branch - later the Suppression Bureau - stepped in to offer an arrangement. Hush House received funding, but submitted to yearly inspections, and also surrendered a portion of the Isle for the Branch's prison.

Data:Period.solar.json.label: Solar Gothic Period
Data:Period.solar.json.desc: From the 11th to the early 16th Century, the sisters and brothers of St Brandan's dwelt on the Isle. It was a holy place, a wealthy place, and a centre of learning - though a surprisingly obscure one. Then in 1534, the Bronze King Henry dissolved the foundation, exiled the brethren, and gave the Isle to the family Dewulf.

Data:Persistent.json.label: Persistent
Data:Persistent.json.desc: Persistent Memories survive the dawn, but when the season called Numa passes, they will depart with it. Numa comes to Brancrug in one season out of every nine - but exactly when is never certain, and years may pass without any sign of Numa's mists.

Data:Pheasant.json.Label: Pheasant
Data:Pheasant.json.Desc: [Roast it, or add Butter if you intend to jug it.]

Data:Pheasant.roast.json.Label: Roast Pheasant
Data:Pheasant.roast.json.Desc: Best when roasted upside down to start, but turned right way up before the end.

Data:Pheasant.roast.salad.grape.json.Label: Cold Pheasant with Grape Salad
Data:Pheasant.roast.salad.grape.json.Desc: This was the sort of dish you might expect to find for a late supper after the theatre, or halfway through a ball.' - Arabella Boxer

Data:Pie.apples.json.Label: Apple Pie
Data:Pie.apples.json.Desc: Flaky, buttery crust; tart-sweet apples with cinnamon and nutmeg.

Data:Pie.cottage.json.Label: Cottage Pie
Data:Pie.cottage.json.Desc: A rich minced beef sauce under a golden crust of baked mash potatoes. Just the thing to come home to after a storm on the moors.

Data:Pie.game.json.Label: Game Pie
Data:Pie.game.json.Desc: Pheasant or snipe or woodcock or rabbit, and tasty pastry.

Data:Pie.kingsluck.json.Label: Kingsluck Pie
Data:Pie.kingsluck.json.Desc: Thirza Blake always insisted on calling it 'the Great Pie of Power', to the lasting annoyance of her peers.

Data:Pie.pears.json.Label: Pear Pie
Data:Pie.pears.json.Desc: Flaky, buttery crust; luscious pears with cinnamon and nutmeg.

xexts.scrutiny: Appetite satisfied.  [If you make this another time, try adding Roast Beef once it's complete.]

Data:Pie.pilchards.json.Label: Starygazy Pie
Data:Pie.pilchards.json.Desc: We are all in the gutter, but some of us are looking at the stars.' - Wilde, Lady Windermere's Fan

Data:Pie.pumpkin.amber.json.Label: Amber Pumpkin Pie
Data:Pie.pumpkin.amber.json.Desc: A favourite of Kitty Mazarine's second son. Of course she had to leave them behind in the place of her birth, but she brought the recipe to Brancrug. Did she remember him each time she baked it? Even until the very end?

Data:Pie.pumpkin.honey.json.Label: Honey-Haunted Pumpkin Pie
Data:Pie.pumpkin.honey.json.Desc: Harvey Hattington, perenially suspicious of the Blomberende-kind and their cuckoo-honey, nevertheless championed pumpkin pie made with cuckoo-honey as 'the Herald of Savour.'

Data:Pie.pumpkin.json.Label: Pumpkin Pie
Data:Pie.pumpkin.json.Desc: Take a pound of pumpion and slice it, a handful of thyme, a little rosemary, and sweet marjoram stripped off the stalks, chop them small, then take cinnamon, nutmeg, pepper, and a few cloves all beaten…' - Hannah Woolley, A Gentlewoman's Companion
